redFirst.basis: Task is gate-only with expectRedFirst false, so the helper was not run. I added dl6 and watched it FAIL on the previous code (RuntimeError surfaced, phase-P1 still held), then green after the fix.

outcome.technical: drive() in drive-phase.py now releases the lock on every exit once taken: a returned stop and a ValueError (converted to a stop) release via the new give_back_lock helper; any other BaseException releases the lock, then re-raises. Cases dl5 (phase vanishes) and dl6 (RuntimeError after lock surfaces and lock is released) in tests/test_drive_phase.py. Selftest 229/229. Exit codes: sweep-selftests.py 0, --spaced 0, ruff 0, vermin 0.
outcome.descriptive: A drive that dies after taking the phase lock, by stop or by any exception, no longer strands the lock.

claims: claims: release_lock failing during exception unwinding is ignored in favour of re-raising the original error (give_back_lock's refusal is not surfaced on that path). dl6 evidence: red then green, 229/229.
